en.title: 1. Elimination Brackets & Match Play
en.excerpt: Complete guide to generating World Archery matchplay trees, set system vs cumulative scoring, automatic medal finals, and bye progressions.

toc.text: 3. Generating Match Trees from Qualification Seeding

en.content:
1. What Are Elimination Brackets?

Elimination brackets represent the head-to-head matchplay phase of an archery tournament. Two athletes go head-to-head on the shooting line, with winners advancing to the next round until the Gold and Bronze medal matches decide the champions on the podium.

2. Bracket Management & Match Overview

To view your tournament's elimination brackets:

  1. Open your tournament in the Organizer Dashboard.
  2. Click Elimination in the left sidebar (/dashboard/organizer/tournaments/[id]/elimination).
  3. Each bracket card displays the division title, scoring rule, slot capacity (e.g., Top 4, Top 8, Top 16, Top 32, Top 64), and a quick link to manage live matches.

3. Generating Match Trees from Qualification Seeding

To generate a new elimination tree:

  1. Click the yellow + Create Elimination Bracket button in the top header.
  2. Select the target Competition Category (e.g., Recurve Men 70m Individual).
  3. Choose the Cutoff Size based on your tournament schedule (e.g., Top 8 for Quarters, Top 16 for 1/8 Round, or Top 32).
  4. Click Generate Bracket Tree. Archeris automatically populates match positions following international World Archery seeding pairing tables (#1 vs #16, #8 vs #9, etc.).

4. Set System (Recurve) vs Cumulative Score (Compound)

Archeris supports both official World Archery scoring modes:

  • Set System (Recurve & Barebow): Matches consist of up to 5 sets (3 arrows per set). The archer with the higher set total earns 2 set points (1 point each for a tie). First archer to reach 6 set points wins the match.
  • Cumulative / Total Score (Compound): Archers shoot 5 ends of 3 arrows (15 arrows total). The archer with the highest cumulative combined score wins.
  • One-Arrow Shoot-Off (Tie Break): If archers remain tied after full sets or cumulative arrows, a single shoot-off arrow is recorded, with the closest arrow to center X winning.

5. Semifinals, Bronze & Gold Medal Matches

When matches reach the final four contenders:

  • Semifinal Winners: Automatically advance to the Gold Medal Final (1st vs 2nd place).
  • Semifinal Losers: Automatically advance to the Bronze Medal Match (3rd vs 4th place).
  • Live Results: Once the final arrow is submitted, official results immediately sync to public tournament brackets, athlete profiles, and printable Result Books!
